# Distillate: Fabrication and errors in the bibliographic citations generated by ChatGPT

The source measures how often two versions of one chatbot invent references outright and how often the references that do exist are cited wrongly, and it is the vault's quantitative base for the claim that an unanchored generated reference cannot be trusted.

## Core statements

- The study used GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 to generate short papers on 42 multidisciplinary topics and compiled data on the 636 bibliographic citations found in the resulting 84 papers. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww11]] ^s1
- Of the 222 works cited in the GPT-3.5 papers, 55% are fabricated, meaning they do not exist as works that have been published, presented, posted or otherwise publicly disseminated. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww24]] ^s2
- Of the works cited by GPT-4, 18% are fabricated, and 70% of the book chapters it cites are fabricated. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww25]] ^s3
- Among the GPT-3.5 cited works that are real, 43% carry one or more substantive citation errors in authorship, title, date, journal title, volume, issue, page numbers or publisher. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww28]] ^s4
- Within the same set of documents, 24% of the real GPT-4 citations include substantive citation errors, against 43% for GPT-3.5. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww01]] ^s5
- A cited work counted as real when a search found an actual work matching or nearly matching in both title and authorship, so that an incorrect citation to an existing work was not counted as a fabrication. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww18]] ^s6
- Each cited work was checked against Google, Google Scholar, Amazon, the Directory of Open Access Journals, PubMed, Scopus, WorldCat and publisher and journal websites. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww17]] ^s7
- Most of the fabricated article, book and website citations name real journals, publishers and organizations, while many fabricated book chapter references name books that do not exist either. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww26]] ^s8
- ChatGPT often responds inaccurately when it is asked to verify the legitimacy of the works it has cited. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww27]] ^s9
- Every citation is in APA format, yet more than 40% of the citations carry minor formatting errors, most often improper title capitalization. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww30]] ^s10
- GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 each supply hyperlinks for fewer than 10% of their citations to real works, links occur more often within fabricated citations, and about a third of the links given for real works are inaccurate. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww31]] ^s11
- Accurate citations provide evidence for claims, let readers evaluate that evidence, establish a context for new empirical work and mark gaps in the literature, and fabricated citations work against each of those goals. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww09]] ^s12

## Terms

- **Fabricated citation**: a bibliographic citation that does not correspond to an actual scholarly work. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww04]]
- **Substantive citation error**: an error in the bibliographic information of a work that does exist, such as incorrect authorship, title, journal, publisher, volume number or pagination, as distinct from a formatting error. [[10_markdown/documents/fabricated-citations-chatgpt-2023#^ww19]]

## Open questions

- The source reports the fabrication rates for one prompt design and one task genre, the short student literature review, and says nothing about how the rates move under prompts that require a retrievable identifier.
- The counting rule treats a wrong citation to an existing work as an error rather than a fabrication, so the reported fabrication rate is a lower bound on the share of citations a reader cannot follow to the work named.

## Appraisal

Peer-reviewed in a broad-scope journal, with a hand-checked dataset and an explicit, conservative counting rule, which is what makes the figures usable as a floor rather than a headline. Its limit for this vault is the model generation it measures; the rates belong to two specific 2023 systems, and the transferable finding is the failure mode, an assertion of a source that the assertion cannot be traced to, not the percentage.
